I enjoy cooking, but I don't like cleaning. So I'm mastering the art of:

Using as few utensils and items of cookware used as possible. I understand the principle of Mise En Place, but geeze.

I cut stuff up, and throw it right into whatever I'm cooking at the appropriate time.

All I can think of when watching a cooking show is, must be nice to have a team of people for the cleanup.

Cooking while you clean is key. I used to work restaurants so I have very good habits about this and you can too.

Everything you use gets washed immediately. For example, if you are waiting 10 minutes for meat to brown, then spend that time washing dishes and cleaning surfaces.

A lot of things are easier to wash while they are still hot. Don't let food harden on your dishes.

Learn to reduce drips and splatters and move like a ninja.

Make full use of things like aluminum foil and parchment paper.

Painters tarp is cheap and so is cardboard. They are both great for eliminating floor messes.

Practicing one pan cooking is also a great way to reduce dishes. I will usually use a wok and a sauce pan and that is it.

Good luck with your cooking. Practice is everything.

My favorite new "convenience" food is overnight oatmeal. I thought my husband would reject it since It's soooo hot in my area and oatmeal is a heartier food that seems more suitable for cold weather. Making your own convenience foods is the best. No worries about weird preservatives.

I like to enjoy oatmeal even too even though I live in the tropics. Also, paired with a citrus juice you get a nice source of iron.

How do you flavor your oat meal? I just use cinnamon and cane sugar with a bit of butter.

All of these can be eaten cold or heated for about 2 min. You can add chia seeds or omit. I use about 1/3 cup oatmeal with an equal part milk. You can use soy, coconut or other milk. Or sub yogurt. Pour cream or half and half ove to serve if desired.

My favorites so far for oatmeal:

Apple cinnamon cranberry raisin:

Add some chia seeds, Granny Smith Apple sliced thin (or sub dried apple) , a few golden raisins and some regular raisins and a few craisins (dried cranberry). A few pecans. Top with brown sugar and a pinch of salt.

Banana Bread oatmeal:

1/2 of a small mashed banana. Some chia seed. Mix in well with the oats. Add a few drops vanilla extract. A few walnuts and pecans. Top with brown sugar, and pinch of salt and a dab of butter, plus a few banana slices.

Cherry maple nut:

A few dried cherries, a couple of drops almond extract, about a tablespoon maple syrup, a sprinkle of brown sugar, some pecans, a dab of butter and a pinch of salt. Chia seed optional.
